questions: Is the reversal operation global (affects all edges in the entire graph) or local (only edges incident to the current vertex)?
Can the reversal operation be performed multiple times, and if so, does each reversal toggle the direction (so two reversals restore original directions)?
Is the cost X incurred each time the reversal operation is performed, regardless of whether the graph's edge directions are already reversed from a previous operation?
Are self-loops (edges where u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, how do they behave under reversal?
When moving along a directed edge, can you choose any outgoing edge from the current vertex, including ones that may have been created by a previous reversal?
Is the goal to minimize the total cost to reach vertex N, or simply to find the cost required by some sequence (implying minimal cost)?
Does the reversal operation happen instantaneously, allowing immediate movement after reversal in the same step/operation?
Are multiple edges between the same pair of vertices allowed, and if so, do they all reverse independently?
